peer_results.rationale: The available candidates for AMD relate to asset impairment measurement (amd_2024_8_D025) and royalty income recognition from a licensing agreement (amd_2024_8_D084). Neither candidate discusses the valuation methodology, useful life determination, or amortization policy for acquired intangible assets, which is the specific topic of the AVGO disclosure.

The available candidates for INTC relate to depreciation and capitalized interest methodology (intc_2024_8_D019) and a reference to a table of amortization expenses (intc_2024_8_D130). While intc_2024_8_D130 mentions amortization, it does not provide the methodology for determining useful lives or valuation approaches for intangible assets comparable to AVGO's description of the relief-from-royalty method and technology-cycle-based useful life assessment. The depreciation candidate is for tangible assets and thus not comparable.

comparisons.peer_topic: Capitalization and Amortization of Product and Process Technology Costs
comparisons.peer_summary: The company capitalizes costs for acquiring product/process technology and patenting, amortizing them straight-line over up to 12.5 years, with amortization duration set to the shorter of the technology's useful life, patent term, or agreement term; fully-amortized assets are then removed from the books.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU disclose the amortization methodology for technology-related intangible assets. AVGO determines the economic useful life for its developed technology based on the technology cycle and cash flows over the forecast period as part of a valuation using the relief-from-royalty method. Similarly, MU capitalizes product and process technology costs and amortizes them on a straight-line basis over the shorter of the estimated useful life of the technology, the patent term, or the agreement term. Both companies link the useful life determination directly to the specific characteristics of the technology and its economic utility.

sentences.text: The economic useful life was determined based on the technology cycle related to each developed technology, as well as the cash flows over the forecast period.
Product and process technology costs are amortized over the shorter of (1) the estimated useful life of the technology, (2) the patent term, or (3) the term of the technology agreement.
